log.msg: Mike, mid-task, adding a second TIER to the tool: not "broken" but "off". (1) Alignment — 3 columns with unequal heights; a heading that does not visually align with the paragraph below it. Compare coordinates and decide which SHOULD align and which are fine not to. (2) Visual hierarchy — can we see the layout at all? Transparent layouts are powerful but often we are missing the background that would carry hierarchy. Two h1s next to each other is distracting. (3) Card padding as a PERCENTAGE OF WIDTH: 20px on a 1000px card looks off. Did we determine the acceptable ratio, document it, and can he click through and SEE it?

Answering (3) honestly: pad_pct is computed as a METRIC but no rule uses it — the cramped rule divides padding by FONT SIZE only, which is why a 1000px card with 20px padding passes. Font size sets the floor for legibility; width sets the floor for proportion, and a box needs both. Fixing, and the answer gets a live clickable page rather than a paragraph.

log.msg: Mike again: (1) double padding — nested padded containers, fine when the background changes for a callout, likely unintended otherwise. (2) padding/margin collisions — is that a normal part of layout? (3) whitespace detection — flag large unused areas. (4) the could-be-off findings should be DEFERRABLE by the user. (5) "for the layout audit, i want to be able to click through to the page, and know exactly what the issue is, and exactly what the fix would be... you could render the same markup, showing how its broken, and showing the fix, side by side? didn't I ask for that earlier?"

He did ask earlier, and what I built was the WHOLE-PAGE version: two scaled iframes of the entire page with the proposal injected into one. That answers "is it different" but not "what exactly is wrong and what exactly fixes it" — the difference is a few pixels somewhere inside a 0.5x screenshot. The right thing is the ELEMENT: find the offending node, clone it twice at natural size, apply the fix to one. Same-origin clones inherit the site stylesheets, so a cloned node renders as itself. Building that.

assign.now: Baseline regenerating; rules pages and skill landed

log.msg: figma-layouts agent landed and its report was accurate. Figma node 80:2916 is a Layout Documentation System — 14 specimens filed by BREAKPOINT, which is the inverse of how this catalog thinks, so it collapsed each pattern into one intrinsic layout. Ten of the fourteen were already words here; it built the four that were not (hero, pricing, carousel, overlay) and wrote ZERO stylesheet CSS. Measured like-for-like at page scope after my fixes: B 81-86 at 1280, B 87-A 90 at 3440, zero high anywhere.

It found two real analyzer bugs, both confirmed and fixed. (1) doc-overflow had no scroller guard — every carousel slide waiting off-screen reported as content past the viewport, which was the sole cause of every high finding in its four pages. false-positives.md already stated the principle and this was the one rule not applying it; carousel went D 62 to B 81. (2) alignment fired on inline-block icons and chips, six times on one page: boxed() lets inline-block through, so a lane is now block-level only. It also flagged that .measure hardcodes margin-inline: auto and cannot be used left-aligned — three of its layouts worked around it with inline max-width, which is exactly the hardcode a utility exists to replace.

Graduated severity did what Mike asked — measure HIGH went 238 to 5 across the site, because 87 characters is no longer treated like 300. But the polish tier immediately drowned the signal it was meant to add: alignment fired 987 med + 1715 low across 120 pages, illegible 362 low, pad-scale 488, hierarchy 273. Five rules each capped at 25 still sum to 125, and grades collapsed to F:106 D:11 C:3 A:1 — every page equally condemned, which is no ranking at all. Same failure mode false-positives.md already names: a rule that fires on the common case is worse than no rule.

Three fixes. (1) The polish tier is now capped TOGETHER at 15 points, not per-rule — a layout that is merely unpolished must not score like one nobody can read. (2) alignment needed 3px and a four-element lane, not 1.5px and three: browsers land fractional edges everywhere and a sub-pixel difference is not a misalignment. (3) illegible now needs real text behind the low tier — a 10px label is a label, a 10px paragraph is a problem — which was every badge, chip and eyebrow on the site.

Final baseline: 242 runs, 0 errors, grades at 1280 now F:20 D:35 C:48 B:17 A:1 — a real spread, where the pre-fix run was F:106 D:11 C:3 A:1. illegible fell 362 to 1, alignment 987 med to 613 (and capped in score regardless). findings.json trimmed to 668KB by keeping issues only for pages under 70 and dropping the low tier from the saved rows.

assign.outcome: **The tool got a second tier, a real address, and a documentation system.** Fixed the audit page own broken layout (the h1 at 0,0 Mike caught) and added the `gutter` rule that would have caught it. Severity is now a CURVE — three thresholds per rule, magnitude picks one — so 87 characters is no longer treated like 300 (measure high went 238 to 5 site-wide). Repeated siblings collapse onto their parent: eight paragraphs at 96 characters is one finding on the container that never bounded them. New polish tier (alignment, pad-scale, double-pad, whitespace, hierarchy, ragged-row, invisible), capped at 15 points together and deferrable per finding. Node addresses are `:nth-child()` paths relative to a recorded root, which is what makes `mirror.js` work: the offending ELEMENT cloned twice at its own size, broken beside fixed. Docs: `framework/styles/rules/` (cascade, proportion, nesting, robust, reuse) with live examples the analyzer measures as they render, plus a `css-strategy` skill. The Figma agent shipped four new layouts (hero, pricing, carousel, overlay) with zero stylesheet CSS and found two real analyzer bugs, both fixed.

log.msg: Mike, on the Wide measure page, four hits and all four correct. (1) "~112.3 characters per line doesnt update in realtime" — the panel WAS recomputing; the METRIC was wrong. chars/lines only moves when the LINE COUNT moves, so a paragraph reported an identical 112.3 at 1207px and at 941px because both wrap to three lines. Now: total inked rect width / chars is the fonts real average advance and does not depend on wrapping, so line width / advance is continuous. Reads 158.4 / 126.8 / 96.2 / 91.8 as the window narrows. (2) Two paragraphs reported separately — FLOCK lowered from 3 to 2. Two paragraphs in one container are not two slips, they are one container. (3) The title/paragraph misalignment: the case wrapper carried a stray inline padding: 2em that stepped the text 32px right of the page title. (4) Inline styles: he is right, and the policy is now stated — inline means THE BREAKAGE and nothing else; every incidental wrapper padding is deleted.

"Why doesnt this layout tool detect this?" — because alignment only looks at NEAR misses, 3-12px, on the theory that a wider gap is a deliberate second column. A heading and the text under it are never two columns. New heading-offset rule takes the wide window (2-96px) by restricting itself to that one relationship. It missed the reported case on the first try because I skipped heading-over-heading as hierarchys problem — but the actual pair was a page TITLE against an h2 inside the padded wrapper. Guard removed; it now names the h1 and the 32px. Site check: 0-3 per page, all real.
